**Rita A. Crundwell** (née **Humphrey**; born January 10, 1953) is an American woman who served as the [comptroller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comptroller "Comptroller") and [treasurer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treasurer "Treasurer") of [Dixon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dixon,_Illinois "Dixon, Illinois"), [Illinois](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illinois "Illinois"), from 1983 to 2012. She was fired and arrested in April 2012 after the discovery that she had [embezzled](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Embezzlement "Embezzlement") $53.7 million from the city of Dixon for over 22 years to support her championship [American Quarter Horse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Quarter_Horse "American Quarter Horse") breeding operation, as well as a lavish lifestyle away from work.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Crundwell#cite_note-Chicago_Tribune_Jenco-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Crundwell#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Crundwell#cite_note-3) Her embezzlement has been described as the largest municipal fraud in U.S. history.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Crundwell#cite_note-4) Crundwell pleaded guilty to her crimes and was sentenced to 19 years and 7 months in prison.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Crundwell#cite_note-Forbes_sentencing-5)

Crundwell used the money to turn her Quarter Horse breeding operation, RC Quarter Horses, into one of the best-known in the country. Her horses won 52 world championships and she was named the leading owner by the [American Quarter Horse Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Quarter_Horse_Association "American Quarter Horse Association") for eight consecutive years prior to her arrest.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Crundwell#cite_note-JencoGrimm-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Crundwell#cite_note-Keyser-7) She spent 8+1⁄2 years (43% of her sentence) in prison before being released in mid-2021 to serve the remainder of her sentence in home confinement. Her sentence was [commuted](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commutation_(law) "Commutation (law)") along with nearly 1500 other people by President Biden on December 12, 2024. Those commuted were people who had been previously transferred from prison to house arrest under the [CARES Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CARES_Act "CARES Act") due to having a high risk of COVID-19.

## Early life and career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Rita_Crundwell&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life and career")]

Born Rita Humphrey, the daughter of Ray and Caroline Humphrey,[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Crundwell#cite_note-Giuliana-8) Crundwell grew up on her family's farm near Dixon,[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Crundwell#cite_note-Keyser-7) and was a student at [Dixon High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dixon_High_School_(Illinois) "Dixon High School (Illinois)"). In 1970, a year before graduating,[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Crundwell#cite_note-Keyser-7) the teenager began working at the Dixon City Hall as a work-study student.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Crundwell#cite_note-Forbes_sentencing-5) She began showing [American Quarter Horses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Quarter_Horse "American Quarter Horse") in 1978.

She married engineering technician Jerry L. Crundwell in 1974, while working as a secretary for Dixon's mayor, but divorced Crundwell in 1986.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Crundwell#cite_note-9)

In 1983, Crundwell was appointed the [treasurer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treasurer "Treasurer") and [comptroller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comptroller "Comptroller") for Dixon, working in this capacity for almost three decades.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Crundwell#cite_note-Forbes_sentencing-5)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Crundwell#cite_note-Keyser-7)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Crundwell#cite_note-10) Crundwell acquired a sterling reputation; in 2011, one of the city commissioners praised her stewardship of city finances, saying that "she looks after every tax dollar as if it were her own."[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Crundwell#cite_note-11)

## Embezzlement

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Rita_Crundwell&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Embezzlement")]

In 1990, Crundwell opened a bank account named the Reserve Sewer Capital Development Account (RSCDA), making it appear to be a city account. She was the only [signatory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Signature "Signature"). Crundwell would have money deposited into another account called the Capital Development Fund, create false state [invoices](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invoice "Invoice"), and then write checks from the fund payable to "Treasurer", which she would deposit into the RSCDA account. According to federal investigators, this relatively uncomplicated scheme continued for 22 years.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Crundwell#cite_note-Forbes_sentencing-5)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Crundwell#cite_note-AmericanGreed-12)

On average, Crundwell stole nearly $2.5 million per year from the city, starting from a low of $181,000 in 1991, growing to the embezzlement of $5.8 million in 2008–from a city with an annual budget of $8–9 million.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Crundwell#cite_note-Forbes_sentencing-5)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Crundwell#cite_note-13) Crundwell used the money not only to finance her Quarter Horse operation, but also to support a lifestyle well beyond her $80,000 city salary, purchasing several cars, a second house[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Crundwell#cite_note-14) and a $2.1 million 45-foot luxury [motorhome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motorhome "Motorhome").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Crundwell#cite_note-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Crundwell#cite_note-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Crundwell#cite_note-17)

Crundwell covered up her [embezzlement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Embezzlement "Embezzlement") by claiming that the city's frequent budget shortfalls were due to the state being late in paying its share of [tax revenue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tax_revenue "Tax revenue").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Crundwell#cite_note-plea-18) She forced city departments to make drastic service cuts to keep the budget within reason. As a result, employees went two years or more without raises and the police department could not afford new radios.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Crundwell#cite_note-19) The most visible effect, however, was on street maintenance; the city was forced to lay off three of its nine street repair workers and cut the rate of maintenance. In the decade before Crundwell's arrest, only 65 blocks of road were repaired or replaced.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Crundwell#cite_note-appeal-20)

For most of Crundwell's tenure, residents assumed either that she inherited her wealth and/or that her horse breeding business was profitable in its own right. However, by the onset of the [Great Recession](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Recession "Great Recession"), some grew suspicious that Crundwell was stealing money. But the city's outside [auditors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Auditor "Auditor"), Clifton Gunderson (now [CliftonLarsonAllen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CliftonLarsonAllen "CliftonLarsonAllen") after merging with LarsonAllen in 2012) and local accountant Samuel Card presumed that Crundwell was honest and signed off on her annual financial statements without concern. For small U.S. cities similar to Dixon, lack of sufficient outside audits was a recurring problem, as third-party auditors could give at best limited attention. For most of her tenure as comptroller, Crundwell had nearly complete control over the city's accounts, while few city employees had access to the city's financial statements.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Crundwell#cite_note-Forbes_sentencing-5)

## Capture and arrest

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Rita_Crundwell&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Capture and arrest")]

In the fall of 2011, while Crundwell was on an extended vacation, city clerk and acting comptroller Kathe Swanson discovered the RSCDA account with 179 deposits and associated checking activity.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Crundwell#cite_note-Keyser-7) Swanson did not recognize the account as a legitimate city account, and alerted Dixon [mayor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mayor "Mayor") James Burke. In turn, Burke contacted the [Federal Bureau of Investigation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Bureau_of_Investigation "Federal Bureau of Investigation") (FBI). For the next six months, Burke and Swanson (whose payroll was controlled by Crundwell) remained silent while the FBI built their case.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Crundwell#cite_note-AmericanGreed-12)

Crundwell arrived for work on April 17, 2012, to find FBI agents waiting for her. She was arrested later that day and was [indicted](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indictment "Indictment") by a federal [grand jury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_jury "Grand jury") for embezzling $53 million in city money over the previous six years.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Crundwell#cite_note-JencoGrimm-6)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Crundwell#cite_note-AmericanGreed-12)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Crundwell#cite_note-21) Crundwell was charged with one count of [wire fraud](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mail_and_wire_fraud "Mail and wire fraud") and released on $4,500 [bail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bail "Bail") the next day.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Crundwell#cite_note-22)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Crundwell#cite_note-23) On May 2, 2012, a superseding indictment charged Crundwell with embezzling $53 million over the prior 22 years.

On November 14, 2012, Crundwell pleaded guilty before Judge [Philip Reinhard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philip_Godfrey_Reinhard "Philip Godfrey Reinhard") to a single count of wire fraud.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Crundwell#cite_note-24) As part of the deal, she also admitted to [money laundering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Money_laundering "Money laundering") by using the embezzled money to finance her horse operation. Crundwell was required to forfeit more than $53.7 million in cash, assets and possessions, equivalent to the amount she stole, which is being used to make full [restitution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Restitution "Restitution") to the city.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Crundwell#cite_note-plea-18) She reportedly told FBI agents that some of the money was spent on her horses and their upkeep. [Prosecutors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prosecutor "Prosecutor") sought the [forfeiture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asset_forfeiture "Asset forfeiture") of her horse farm and 300 horses, in addition to her three homes and a luxury motorhome vehicle.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Crundwell#cite_note-JencoGrimm-6) Prosecutors later discovered that Crundwell's crimes had begun as early as 1988, when she siphoned off $25,000 from the Dixon Sister City program over two years.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Crundwell#cite_note-Chicago_Tribune_Jenco-1) Had she not pleaded guilty, she would have faced additional charges of [bank fraud](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bank_fraud "Bank fraud"), wire fraud, and money laundering that could have sent her to prison for the rest of her life.

The following month, Dixon's new finance director said that the city had seen an almost $3 million rebound since Crundwell's arrest, but that the operating budget was still off by $16.6 million.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Crundwell#cite_note-Peoria_Journal_Star_budget_rebounding-25) It was also reported that Dixon lost $30 million in operating funds over the prior decade.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Crundwell#cite_note-Peoria_Journal_Star_budget_rebounding-25) The city sued its outside auditors, as well as the city's banker, [Fifth Third Bank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifth_Third_Bank "Fifth Third Bank"), for ignoring numerous red flags in Crundwell's actions. In September 2013, the auditors and Fifth Third agreed to pay the city $40 million in a [legal settlement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Settlement_(litigation) "Settlement (litigation)"), while the auction of Crundwell's assets brought in over $9 million.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Crundwell#cite_note-26) Richard Humphrey Jr., Crundwell's nephew, purchased the 88-acre (36 ha) horse ranch formerly owned by Crundwell, for $1 million in an auction a few days before she was sentenced.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Crundwell#cite_note-27) Her brother, Richard, purchased one of the houses she owned in Dixon.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Crundwell#cite_note-28) The property includes 40 acres (16 ha) of farmland that borders another 40 acres of farmland he owns.

At sentencing on February 14, 2013, prosecutors sought the maximum sentence of 20 years in federal prison. Their case was bolstered by testimony from Burke and city staffers that Crundwell used dramatic analogies to force spending cuts to cover up her theft, which left Dixon unable to provide the most basic services. The [defense](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Defense_(legal) "Defense (legal)") asked for 13 years, saying that Crundwell had cooperated with authorities in recovering the money. Ultimately, Reinhard sentenced Crundwell to 19 years and 7 months in prison, close to what prosecutors had sought. Reinhard noted that she put her passion for raising horses ahead of the needs of the city residents who had entrusted her with their funds, and that a significant prison term was required to restore public confidence. Reinhard was so disgusted with Crundwell's behavior that he revoked her bail and remanded her to custody rather than allow her to self-report to prison.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Crundwell#cite_note-Forbes_sentencing-5)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Crundwell#cite_note-Chicago_Tribune_Jenco-1)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Crundwell#cite_note-appeal-20)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Crundwell#cite_note-Peoria_Journal_Star_Babwin-29) Crundwell [appealed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Appeal "Appeal") the sentence, but the [Seventh Circuit Court of Appeals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Court_of_Appeals_for_the_Seventh_Circuit "United States Court of Appeals for the Seventh Circuit") upheld it in November 2013.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Crundwell#cite_note-appeal-20)

Crundwell's embezzlement has been the subject of academic and professional publications.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Crundwell#cite_note-30)

On September 20, 2012, Crundwell was also indicted on 60 state counts of theft, alleging that she stole $11.2 million from April 2010 until the day of her arrest. Burke and [Lee County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lee_County,_Illinois "Lee County, Illinois") State's Attorney Henry Dixon said the state charges, which carried a minimum of 6 years per count, were a backup in case Crundwell was [acquitted](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acquittal "Acquittal") on the federal charges.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Crundwell#cite_note-31) The state charges were dropped in April 2013. Dixon's successor as state's attorney, Anna Sacco-Miller, said that it did not make sense to spend taxpayer money on prosecuting Crundwell, as there were virtually no assets left for the state to seize (though Dixon had initially said he had no plans to seize assets from her). Sacco-Miller also said that because Illinois sentencing guidelines require state and federal sentences to run concurrently, Crundwell would likely serve out any sentence imposed at the state level while she was still in federal prison.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Crundwell#cite_note-32)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Crundwell#cite_note-33)

## Prison and release

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Rita_Crundwell&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Prison and release")]

Crundwell was incarcerated at minimum-security [Federal Correctional Institution, Waseca](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Correctional_Institution,_Waseca "Federal Correctional Institution, Waseca") in [Waseca, Minnesota](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waseca,_Minnesota "Waseca, Minnesota"). She was originally eligible and scheduled for release after serving 85% of her sentence (16 years 8 months) on March 5, 2030.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Crundwell#cite_note-34) Under the [First Step Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Step_Act "First Step Act") she was receiving [good conduct time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Good_conduct_time "Good conduct time") deductions of 54 days per year off her sentence.

On April 27, 2020, Crundwell submitted a request for a compassionate release with the warden of the Federal Prison Camp in Waseca. On that same date she filed a motion with the Illinois Northern District Court in Rockford, Illinois.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Crundwell#cite_note-letter-35) Her motion requested home confinement under the First Step Act. The motion also sought a transfer to home confinement based on a [Response to the COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Impact_of_the_COVID-19_pandemic_on_prisons "Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on prisons") memo dated March 26, 2020, from Attorney General [William Barr](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Barr "William Barr") to the [Federal Bureau of Prisons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Bureau_of_Prisons "Federal Bureau of Prisons"). Crundwell cited, amongst other things, her "health issues, including high blood pressure and high cholesterol"[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Crundwell#cite_note-letter-35)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Crundwell#cite_note-downersgrove-36) and her good conduct while incarcerated. The motion was withdrawn by Crundwell on May 18, 2020, a few days after Dixon City Council strongly opposed an early release. The motion withdrawing the home confinement request was granted on May 21, 2020.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Crundwell#cite_note-37)

A little over a year later, on August 4, 2021, after serving half of the required 45% of her sentence (about 8+1⁄2 years), she was released by the Federal Bureau of Prisons (i.e. not by a court) on compassionate grounds to a _residential reentry center_ - a [halfway house](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Halfway_house "Halfway house")[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Crundwell#cite_note-38) or a home confinement,[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Crundwell#cite_note-39) possibly her brother, Richard Humphrey's ranch (farm[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Crundwell#cite_note-letter-35)) in Dixon as she proposed in her previously withdrawn request for release.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Crundwell#cite_note-houseconfinement-40) Two months later in October 2021, she was reported to live at the brother's 80-acre farm.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Crundwell#cite_note-BackInDixon-41) Because she is serving her sentence in home confinement, she's not allowed to leave the farm property without permission. She was overseen by a residential reentry management field office in Chicago suburb [Downers Grove](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Downers_Grove,_Illinois "Downers Grove, Illinois").[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Crundwell#cite_note-downersgrove-36)

On December 12, 2024, Crundwell's sentence was commuted by President [Joe Biden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Biden "Joe Biden") along with nearly 1500 other individuals who were previously released under the CARES Act, which allowed people with a high risk of COVID-19 to be released from prison into home detention.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Crundwell#cite_note-m490-42)

Crundwell's story was featured on the January 15, 2025, edition of [Freeform](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freeform_(TV_channel) "Freeform (TV channel)")'s _Scam Goddess_, hosted by [Laci Mosley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laci_Mosley "Laci Mosley").[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Crundwell#cite_note-43)

**David Henry Dewhurst** (born August 18, 1945) is an American politician, businessman, and attorney who served as the 41st [lieutenant governor of Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lieutenant_governor_of_Texas "Lieutenant governor of Texas") from 2003 to 2015. A member of the [Republican Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_Party_(United_States) "Republican Party (United States)"), he was the [Texas Land Commissioner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_General_Land_Office "Texas General Land Office") from 1999 to 2003. He was a candidate in 2012 for the [U.S. Senate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Senate "U.S. Senate") seat vacated by the retiring Republican [Kay Bailey Hutchison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kay_Bailey_Hutchison "Kay Bailey Hutchison"), but he lost his party's [runoff election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Runoff_election "Runoff election") to former [Solicitor General](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solicitor_General_of_Texas "Solicitor General of Texas")[Ted Cruz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_Cruz "Ted Cruz"), who went on to win the [general election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_election "General election"). Dewhurst ran for a fourth term as Lieutenant Governor in 2014, but lost renomination to then-state senator [Dan Patrick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Patrick_(politician) "Dan Patrick (politician)") in the Republican primary.

Dewhurst's third term as lieutenant governor ended on January 20, 2015. He served as an advisory board member at the [United States Secretary of Energy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_Energy "United States Secretary of Energy") led by former Governor [Rick Perry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry "Rick Perry") who was appointed by [President](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_United_States "President of the United States")[Donald Trump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump "Donald Trump") in 2017.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Dewhurst#cite_note-3)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=David_Dewhurst&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Dewhurst's father, David Dewhurst Jr., was a World War II pilot of a [Martin B-26 Marauder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martin_B-26_Marauder "Martin B-26 Marauder") of the [553d Fighter-Bomber Squadron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/553d_Fighter-Bomber_Squadron "553d Fighter-Bomber Squadron"). On D-Day, flying over [Cotentin Peninsula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cotentin_Peninsula "Cotentin Peninsula") in the "Dinah Might", he led a squadron bombing German positions on [Utah Beach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Utah_Beach "Utah Beach"). After the war, David Dewhurst Jr. was killed by a drunk driver, leaving behind his wife and his two sons, David and Eugene.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Dewhurst#cite_note-TM1-4)

Both brothers visited the Utah Beach Museum on June 7, 2007, and discovered an exhibit detailing their father's mission on D-Day. Moved, the Dewhurst brothers contributed millions of dollars for the extension of the museum, allowing it to purchase a B-26 Marauder and to open a new building.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Dewhurst#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Dewhurst#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Dewhurst#cite_note-7)

Dewhurst is a businessman, a [rancher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rancher "Rancher"), and a community leader in Houston, where he has served on civic and charitable boards. He graduated from [Lamar High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lamar_High_School_(Houston) "Lamar High School (Houston)") in Houston[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Dewhurst#cite_note-HISDAlumni-8) and earned his bachelor's degree and played [basketball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basketball "Basketball") at the [University of Arizona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Arizona "University of Arizona") in [Tucson, Arizona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tucson,_Arizona "Tucson, Arizona"), where he was a brother of the [Beta Theta Pi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beta_Theta_Pi "Beta Theta Pi") fraternity. There he received a [BA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachelor_of_Arts "Bachelor of Arts") in English with a minor in history.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Dewhurst#cite_note-TM1-4)

Lacking the eyesight to become a pilot like his father, Dewhurst became an [intelligence officer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intelligence_officer "Intelligence officer") in the [U.S. Air Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Air_Force "U.S. Air Force")[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Dewhurst#cite_note-TM1-4) and then an officer of the [Central Intelligence Agency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Intelligence_Agency "Central Intelligence Agency"),[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Dewhurst#cite_note-9) and the [United States State Department](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_State_Department "United States State Department"). During his years in the CIA, Dewhurst was stationed in Bolivia, arriving shortly before the coup against leftist president [Juan José Torres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juan_Jos%C3%A9_Torres "Juan José Torres").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Dewhurst#cite_note-TM1-4)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Dewhurst#cite_note-TO1-10)

In 1981, Dewhurst and Ted Law re-established Falcon Seaboard, a Texas-based diversified energy and investments company in Houston that Law had founded in 1935.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Dewhurst#cite_note-11) The company quickly made Dewhurst a millionaire, but collapsed just as quickly, going into bankruptcy. Dewhurst then went into business constructing [cogeneration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cogeneration "Cogeneration") plants, which proved to be a tremendous success. In 1996, the company sold its plants for $226 million, and in 2011, Dewhurst was worth an estimated $200 million.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Dewhurst#cite_note-TM1-4)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Dewhurst#cite_note-12)

In 1995, Dewhurst married Tammy Jo Hopkins, a 32-year-old model. After she pled [no contest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No_contest "No contest") to [driving while intoxicated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Driving_while_intoxicated "Driving while intoxicated") in 1999, the couple announced that she would seek full-time help for alcohol abuse. The couple divorced in 2000.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Dewhurst#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Dewhurst#cite_note-DN1-14)

In April 2021, Dewhurst was arrested on charges of domestic violence at a Dallas hotel. The arrest record said Dewhurst was trying to board a bus back to Houston when he realized his girlfriend, Leslie Caron, 41, had taken his laptop. She ran with it and he chased her onto a patio area near the hotel entrance trying to retrieve his laptop computer, when she fell over a concrete bench. In May 2021, the Dallas County District Attorney's Office declined to accept a domestic violence case against the former lieutenant governor, and no further action was taken.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Dewhurst#cite_note-15)

He breeds registered [Black Angus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Angus "Black Angus") cattle and once competed in National Cutting Horse Association competitions.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Dewhurst#cite_note-16) He also speaks [Spanish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_language "Spanish language").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Dewhurst#cite_note-17)

## Political career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=David_Dewhurst&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Political career")]

### Land Commissioner

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=David_Dewhurst&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Land Commissioner")]

Dewhurst was elected as Commissioner of the General Land Office of Texas in 1998, when the 16-year [incumbent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Incumbent "Incumbent"), [Garry Mauro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garry_Mauro "Garry Mauro"), waged an unsuccessful campaign for [governor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governor_of_Texas "Governor of Texas") against [George W. Bush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush "George W. Bush"). Dewhurst was opposed in the general election by Democratic State Representative [Richard Raymond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Raymond_(Texas_politician) "Richard Raymond (Texas politician)"), then of [Benavides](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benavides,_Texas "Benavides, Texas") and thereafter of [Laredo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laredo,_Texas "Laredo, Texas"). Dewhurst described himself as a "George Bush Republican" and drew on his personal wealth to spend a record $8 million on his run for office (previous candidates for land commissioner had generally spent only $1 million).[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Dewhurst#cite_note-TO1-10)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Dewhurst#cite_note-DN1-14) The campaign was a bitter one, in which Dewhurst's Republican primary opponent, [Jerry E. Patterson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerry_E._Patterson "Jerry E. Patterson"), accused Dewhurst of trying to bribe him to leave the race, and Raymond unsuccessfully accused him of [embezzlement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Embezzlement "Embezzlement").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Dewhurst#cite_note-TM1-4) Dewhurst ultimately received 2,072,604 votes (57.42 percent) to Raymond's 1,438,378 ballots (39.85 percent).[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Dewhurst#cite_note-18)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Dewhurst#cite_note-19) Dewhurst was the first Republican to serve as Land Commissioner since the Reconstruction era.

### Lieutenant governor

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=David_Dewhurst&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Lieutenant governor")]

#### 2002 election

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=David_Dewhurst&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: 2002 election")]

Dewhurst was elected lieutenant governor in November 2002, when he defeated former Democratic Comptroller [John Sharp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Sharp_(Texas_politician) "John Sharp (Texas politician)") of [Victoria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victoria,_Texas "Victoria, Texas"), now the chancellor of [Texas A&M University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_A&M_University "Texas A&M University"). In that campaign, Dewhurst stressed his interest in public education and opposition to [school vouchers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/School_voucher "School voucher"). He again outspent his opponent significantly with a $9 million campaign.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Dewhurst#cite_note-TO1-10) Dewhurst polled 2,341,875 votes (51.77 percent) to Sharp's 2,082,281 (46.03 percent).[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Dewhurst#cite_note-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Dewhurst#cite_note-21)

Dewhurst succeeded [Bill Ratliff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Ratliff "Bill Ratliff"). (Ratliff did not contest the lieutenant governor's position in the primary, opting instead for re-election to his state senate seat.)

Summarizing Dewhurst's first term, _[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_New\_York\_Times "The New York Times")_ wrote, "Amid low expectations, Mr. Dewhurst surprised many that first session, helping to steer a major tort-reform package and cutting the budget while earning the respect of his colleagues as a burgeoning team player." However, the paper also noted that he "frequently frustrated senators from both parties for not appearing to hold firm in negotiations with the House or with [Gov. Rick] Perry."[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Dewhurst#cite_note-22)

#### 2006 election

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=David_Dewhurst&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: 2006 election")]

Dewhurst was renominated for lieutenant governor in the Republican primary held on March 7, 2006. He defeated Tom Kelly, the same candidate whom he bested for the nomination in 2002. In the November 7, 2006, general election, Dewhurst overwhelmed Democrat Maria Luisa Alvarado, a veterans issues research analyst and the winner of her April 11 runoff primary. He received 2,512,197 votes (58.2 percent) to Alvarado's 1,616,945 (37.4 percent). Libertarian Judy A. Baker polled another 188,956 votes (4.4 percent).

#### 2010 election

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=David_Dewhurst&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: 2010 election")]

Dewhurst filed for Lt. Governor of Texas in the 2010 election.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Dewhurst#cite_note-23) It was widely assumed that he would run for United States Senate if [Kay Bailey Hutchison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kay_Bailey_Hutchison "Kay Bailey Hutchison") had resigned.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Dewhurst#cite_note-24) He was his party's nominee for a third term as lieutenant governor and faced Democrat Linda Chavez-Thompson,[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Dewhurst#cite_note-Fikac-25)[Libertarian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Libertarian_Party_(United_States) "Libertarian Party (United States)") Scott Jameson,[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Dewhurst#cite_note-libcandidates-26) and [Green Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_Party_(United_States) "Green Party (United States)") Herb Gonzales, Jr.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Dewhurst#cite_note-greencandidates-27) in the November 2, 2010, [general election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_election "General election"). He was re-elected to a third term on November 2, 2010, having polled 3,044,770 votes (61.80 percent) to the [Democrat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Party_(United_States) "Democratic Party (United States)")[Linda Chavez-Thompson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linda_Chavez-Thompson "Linda Chavez-Thompson")'s 1,715,735 votes (34.82 percent) and took office on January 18, 2011, for a third four-year term, becoming the second Texas Lieutenant Governor to be elected to three four-year terms since [Bill Hobby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Hobby "Bill Hobby"), who held the office for 18 years for five terms.

#### 2014 election

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=David_Dewhurst&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: 2014 election")]

Dewhurst and Patrick faced each other in the May 27 runoff election for lieutenant governor. The winner would eventually run in the general election against Democratic State Senator [Leticia Van de Putte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leticia_Van_de_Putte "Leticia Van de Putte") of [San Antonio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Antonio,_Texas "San Antonio, Texas"), who was the Democratic nominee for the lieutenant governorship. During the runoff, Dewhurst released a disco-themed advertisement [Lt. Gov. You've Gotta Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lt._Gov._You've_Gotta_Love "Lt. Gov. You've Gotta Love") and [a parody](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frozen_(advertisement) "Frozen (advertisement)") of [Let It Go](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Let_It_Go_(Disney_song) "Let It Go (Disney song)") from the [Disney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Walt_Disney_Company "The Walt Disney Company") film _[Frozen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frozen\_(2013\_film) "Frozen (2013 film)")_. On May 27, 2014, Patrick easily defeated Dewhurst in a landslide: 65% to 35%.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Dewhurst#cite_note-28)

Patrick said after state Senator [Wendy Davis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wendy_Davis_(politician) "Wendy Davis (politician)") of [Fort Worth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Worth "Fort Worth") (who was the Democratic nominee for governor) [filibustered](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filibuster "Filibuster") the bill to ban late-term abortions in Texas that Dewhurst has "lost his grip on the reins of the Senate". Patrick called for new leadership in the chamber.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Dewhurst#cite_note-davisfilibuster-29)

Polling by the [University of Texas at Austin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Texas_at_Austin "University of Texas at Austin") and _[The Texas Tribune](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Texas\_Tribune "The Texas Tribune")_ showed Dewhurst leading his opponents in the primary with 26 percent of the vote, to Patrick's 13 percent, Patterson's 10 percent and Staples' 5 percent. At the time, 46 percent of voters were reported as undecided.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Dewhurst#cite_note-30)

### Legislation

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=David_Dewhurst&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Legislation")]

#### Childhood legislation

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=David_Dewhurst&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Childhood legislation")]

He is known by his "Texas Children First" initiative[_[clarification needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Please\_clarify "Wikipedia:Please clarify")_] with more severe consequences for child sexual predators in Texas and throughout the [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States "United States").[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Dewhurst#cite_note-31) The initiative includes extending [statute of limitations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statute_of_limitations "Statute of limitations") on child sex crimes and leading the passage of [Jessica's Law](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jessica's_Law "Jessica's Law"). The bill was signed into law by Texas Governor [Rick Perry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry "Rick Perry") but the death penalty for second-time child rapists was struck down by the [U.S. Supreme Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Supreme_Court "U.S. Supreme Court").[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Dewhurst#cite_note-32)

#### TSA inspection bill

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=David_Dewhurst&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: TSA inspection bill")]

Dewhurst was accused by state senator Dan Patrick of helping to stop a bill, the passage of which would have been an attempt to make the pat downs of airplane passengers by personnel of the U.S. Transportation Security Agency (TSA) a felony in Texas.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Dewhurst#cite_note-33)

### Controversies

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=David_Dewhurst&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Controversies")]

#### Condemnation of school stage play

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=David_Dewhurst&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Condemnation of school stage play")]

In March 2010, a student performance of the play _[Corpus Christi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corpus\_Christi\_(play) "Corpus Christi (play)")_ by [Terrence McNally](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terrence_McNally "Terrence McNally"), in which Jesus and the disciples are portrayed as being gay, was canceled at [Tarleton State University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tarleton_State_University "Tarleton State University") in [Stephenville, Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephenville,_Texas "Stephenville, Texas") following a condemnatory statement by Dewhurst. The university had received many complaints about the play's scheduled performance as a class project for a directing class, but in a letter posted on the university's website on March 11, President F. Dominic Dottavio, citing freedom of speech, declared that the play would be performed.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Dewhurst#cite_note-34) The day before the performance, Dewhurst issued his statement saying, "No one should have the right to use government funds or institutions to portray acts that are morally reprehensible to the vast majority of Americans," and the performance was cancelled by the professor, who cited safety concerns. A subsequent statement by Dewhurst praised the university for canceling the performance, whereas the professor claimed to have acted on his own. Dewhurst's statement also claimed that whereas he is "a strong defender of free speech, we must also protect the rights and reasonable expectations of Texas taxpayers and how their money is used. A play that is completely contrary to the standards of decency and moral beliefs of the vast majority of Texans should not be performed using any state resources, especially by an institution of higher learning."[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Dewhurst#cite_note-35)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Dewhurst#cite_note-36)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Dewhurst#cite_note-37)

#### Calling Allen, Texas police regarding jailed relative

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=David_Dewhurst&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Calling Allen, Texas police regarding jailed relative")]

In an August 3, 2013, recording, originally released by police to the Dallas-Fort Worth NBC affiliate, NBC-DFW, Dewhurst identifies himself as the lieutenant governor and asks to speak to the police station's "most senior police officer you have where you are right now". He tells a police sergeant that Ellen Bevers, his stepsister's daughter-in-law, is a schoolteacher and "the sweetest woman in the world", and says he's sure she has been incarcerated on a "mistaken charge".[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Dewhurst#cite_note-38)[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Dewhurst#cite_note-39)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Dewhurst#cite_note-40)

## 2012 United States Senate race

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=David_Dewhurst&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: 2012 United States Senate race")]

See also: [United States Senate election in Texas, 2012](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Senate_election_in_Texas,_2012 "United States Senate election in Texas, 2012")

On July 18, 2011, Dewhurst addressed his supporters in an online video on his campaign website, announcing his candidacy for the vacant U.S. Senate seat for the Republican nomination. His rivals included former [Mayor of Dallas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mayor_of_Dallas "Mayor of Dallas")[Tom Leppert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Leppert "Tom Leppert"), [ESPN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ESPN "ESPN") college football analyst [Craig James](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Craig_James_(running_back) "Craig James (running back)") and former state Solicitor General [Ted Cruz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_Cruz "Ted Cruz"), the eventual nominee.

After a year-long campaign for the Republican nomination, Dewhurst lost to Cruz in a run-off on July 31, 2012. Cruz then won the seat in the general election against Democrat [Paul Sadler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Sadler "Paul Sadler") of [Henderson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henderson,_Texas "Henderson, Texas").

**David Henry Dewhurst** (born August 18, 1945) is an American politician, businessman, and attorney who served as the 41st [lieutenant governor of Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lieutenant_governor_of_Texas "Lieutenant governor of Texas") from 2003 to 2015. A member of the [Republican Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_Party_(United_States) "Republican Party (United States)"), he was the [Texas Land Commissioner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_General_Land_Office "Texas General Land Office") from 1999 to 2003. He was a candidate in 2012 for the [U.S. Senate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Senate "U.S. Senate") seat vacated by the retiring Republican [Kay Bailey Hutchison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kay_Bailey_Hutchison "Kay Bailey Hutchison"), but he lost his party's [runoff election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Runoff_election "Runoff election") to former [Solicitor General](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solicitor_General_of_Texas "Solicitor General of Texas")[Ted Cruz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_Cruz "Ted Cruz"), who went on to win the [general election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_election "General election"). Dewhurst ran for a fourth term as Lieutenant Governor in 2014, but lost renomination to then-state senator [Dan Patrick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Patrick_(politician) "Dan Patrick (politician)") in the Republican primary.

Dewhurst's third term as lieutenant governor ended on January 20, 2015. He served as an advisory board member at the [United States Secretary of Energy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_Energy "United States Secretary of Energy") led by former Governor [Rick Perry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry "Rick Perry") who was appointed by [President](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_United_States "President of the United States")[Donald Trump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump "Donald Trump") in 2017.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Dewhurst#cite_note-3)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=David_Dewhurst&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Dewhurst's father, David Dewhurst Jr., was a World War II pilot of a [Martin B-26 Marauder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martin_B-26_Marauder "Martin B-26 Marauder") of the [553d Fighter-Bomber Squadron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/553d_Fighter-Bomber_Squadron "553d Fighter-Bomber Squadron"). On D-Day, flying over [Cotentin Peninsula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cotentin_Peninsula "Cotentin Peninsula") in the "Dinah Might", he led a squadron bombing German positions on [Utah Beach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Utah_Beach "Utah Beach"). After the war, David Dewhurst Jr. was killed by a drunk driver, leaving behind his wife and his two sons, David and Eugene.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Dewhurst#cite_note-TM1-4)

Both brothers visited the Utah Beach Museum on June 7, 2007, and discovered an exhibit detailing their father's mission on D-Day. Moved, the Dewhurst brothers contributed millions of dollars for the extension of the museum, allowing it to purchase a B-26 Marauder and to open a new building.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Dewhurst#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Dewhurst#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Dewhurst#cite_note-7)

Dewhurst is a businessman, a [rancher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rancher "Rancher"), and a community leader in Houston, where he has served on civic and charitable boards. He graduated from [Lamar High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lamar_High_School_(Houston) "Lamar High School (Houston)") in Houston[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Dewhurst#cite_note-HISDAlumni-8) and earned his bachelor's degree and played [basketball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basketball "Basketball") at the [University of Arizona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Arizona "University of Arizona") in [Tucson, Arizona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tucson,_Arizona "Tucson, Arizona"), where he was a brother of the [Beta Theta Pi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beta_Theta_Pi "Beta Theta Pi") fraternity. There he received a [BA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachelor_of_Arts "Bachelor of Arts") in English with a minor in history.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Dewhurst#cite_note-TM1-4)

Lacking the eyesight to become a pilot like his father, Dewhurst became an [intelligence officer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intelligence_officer "Intelligence officer") in the [U.S. Air Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Air_Force "U.S. Air Force")[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Dewhurst#cite_note-TM1-4) and then an officer of the [Central Intelligence Agency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Intelligence_Agency "Central Intelligence Agency"),[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Dewhurst#cite_note-9) and the [United States State Department](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_State_Department "United States State Department"). During his years in the CIA, Dewhurst was stationed in Bolivia, arriving shortly before the coup against leftist president [Juan José Torres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juan_Jos%C3%A9_Torres "Juan José Torres").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Dewhurst#cite_note-TM1-4)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Dewhurst#cite_note-TO1-10)

In 1981, Dewhurst and Ted Law re-established Falcon Seaboard, a Texas-based diversified energy and investments company in Houston that Law had founded in 1935.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Dewhurst#cite_note-11) The company quickly made Dewhurst a millionaire, but collapsed just as quickly, going into bankruptcy. Dewhurst then went into business constructing [cogeneration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cogeneration "Cogeneration") plants, which proved to be a tremendous success. In 1996, the company sold its plants for $226 million, and in 2011, Dewhurst was worth an estimated $200 million.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Dewhurst#cite_note-TM1-4)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Dewhurst#cite_note-12)

In 1995, Dewhurst married Tammy Jo Hopkins, a 32-year-old model. After she pled [no contest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No_contest "No contest") to [driving while intoxicated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Driving_while_intoxicated "Driving while intoxicated") in 1999, the couple announced that she would seek full-time help for alcohol abuse. The couple divorced in 2000.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Dewhurst#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Dewhurst#cite_note-DN1-14)

In April 2021, Dewhurst was arrested on charges of domestic violence at a Dallas hotel. The arrest record said Dewhurst was trying to board a bus back to Houston when he realized his girlfriend, Leslie Caron, 41, had taken his laptop. She ran with it and he chased her onto a patio area near the hotel entrance trying to retrieve his laptop computer, when she fell over a concrete bench. In May 2021, the Dallas County District Attorney's Office declined to accept a domestic violence case against the former lieutenant governor, and no further action was taken.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Dewhurst#cite_note-15)

He breeds registered [Black Angus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Angus "Black Angus") cattle and once competed in National Cutting Horse Association competitions.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Dewhurst#cite_note-16) He also speaks [Spanish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_language "Spanish language").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Dewhurst#cite_note-17)

## Political career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=David_Dewhurst&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Political career")]

### Land Commissioner

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=David_Dewhurst&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Land Commissioner")]

Dewhurst was elected as Commissioner of the General Land Office of Texas in 1998, when the 16-year [incumbent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Incumbent "Incumbent"), [Garry Mauro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garry_Mauro "Garry Mauro"), waged an unsuccessful campaign for [governor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governor_of_Texas "Governor of Texas") against [George W. Bush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush "George W. Bush"). Dewhurst was opposed in the general election by Democratic State Representative [Richard Raymond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Raymond_(Texas_politician) "Richard Raymond (Texas politician)"), then of [Benavides](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benavides,_Texas "Benavides, Texas") and thereafter of [Laredo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laredo,_Texas "Laredo, Texas"). Dewhurst described himself as a "George Bush Republican" and drew on his personal wealth to spend a record $8 million on his run for office (previous candidates for land commissioner had generally spent only $1 million).[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Dewhurst#cite_note-TO1-10)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Dewhurst#cite_note-DN1-14) The campaign was a bitter one, in which Dewhurst's Republican primary opponent, [Jerry E. Patterson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerry_E._Patterson "Jerry E. Patterson"), accused Dewhurst of trying to bribe him to leave the race, and Raymond unsuccessfully accused him of [embezzlement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Embezzlement "Embezzlement").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Dewhurst#cite_note-TM1-4) Dewhurst ultimately received 2,072,604 votes (57.42 percent) to Raymond's 1,438,378 ballots (39.85 percent).[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Dewhurst#cite_note-18)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Dewhurst#cite_note-19) Dewhurst was the first Republican to serve as Land Commissioner since the Reconstruction era.

### Lieutenant governor

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=David_Dewhurst&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Lieutenant governor")]

#### 2002 election

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=David_Dewhurst&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: 2002 election")]

Dewhurst was elected lieutenant governor in November 2002, when he defeated former Democratic Comptroller [John Sharp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Sharp_(Texas_politician) "John Sharp (Texas politician)") of [Victoria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victoria,_Texas "Victoria, Texas"), now the chancellor of [Texas A&M University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_A&M_University "Texas A&M University"). In that campaign, Dewhurst stressed his interest in public education and opposition to [school vouchers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/School_voucher "School voucher"). He again outspent his opponent significantly with a $9 million campaign.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Dewhurst#cite_note-TO1-10) Dewhurst polled 2,341,875 votes (51.77 percent) to Sharp's 2,082,281 (46.03 percent).[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Dewhurst#cite_note-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Dewhurst#cite_note-21)

Dewhurst succeeded [Bill Ratliff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Ratliff "Bill Ratliff"). (Ratliff did not contest the lieutenant governor's position in the primary, opting instead for re-election to his state senate seat.)

Summarizing Dewhurst's first term, _[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_New\_York\_Times "The New York Times")_ wrote, "Amid low expectations, Mr. Dewhurst surprised many that first session, helping to steer a major tort-reform package and cutting the budget while earning the respect of his colleagues as a burgeoning team player." However, the paper also noted that he "frequently frustrated senators from both parties for not appearing to hold firm in negotiations with the House or with [Gov. Rick] Perry."[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Dewhurst#cite_note-22)

#### 2006 election

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=David_Dewhurst&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: 2006 election")]

Dewhurst was renominated for lieutenant governor in the Republican primary held on March 7, 2006. He defeated Tom Kelly, the same candidate whom he bested for the nomination in 2002. In the November 7, 2006, general election, Dewhurst overwhelmed Democrat Maria Luisa Alvarado, a veterans issues research analyst and the winner of her April 11 runoff primary. He received 2,512,197 votes (58.2 percent) to Alvarado's 1,616,945 (37.4 percent). Libertarian Judy A. Baker polled another 188,956 votes (4.4 percent).

#### 2010 election

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=David_Dewhurst&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: 2010 election")]

Dewhurst filed for Lt. Governor of Texas in the 2010 election.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Dewhurst#cite_note-23) It was widely assumed that he would run for United States Senate if [Kay Bailey Hutchison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kay_Bailey_Hutchison "Kay Bailey Hutchison") had resigned.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Dewhurst#cite_note-24) He was his party's nominee for a third term as lieutenant governor and faced Democrat Linda Chavez-Thompson,[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Dewhurst#cite_note-Fikac-25)[Libertarian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Libertarian_Party_(United_States) "Libertarian Party (United States)") Scott Jameson,[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Dewhurst#cite_note-libcandidates-26) and [Green Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_Party_(United_States) "Green Party (United States)") Herb Gonzales, Jr.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Dewhurst#cite_note-greencandidates-27) in the November 2, 2010, [general election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_election "General election"). He was re-elected to a third term on November 2, 2010, having polled 3,044,770 votes (61.80 percent) to the [Democrat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Party_(United_States) "Democratic Party (United States)")[Linda Chavez-Thompson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linda_Chavez-Thompson "Linda Chavez-Thompson")'s 1,715,735 votes (34.82 percent) and took office on January 18, 2011, for a third four-year term, becoming the second Texas Lieutenant Governor to be elected to three four-year terms since [Bill Hobby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Hobby "Bill Hobby"), who held the office for 18 years for five terms.

#### 2014 election

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=David_Dewhurst&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: 2014 election")]

Dewhurst and Patrick faced each other in the May 27 runoff election for lieutenant governor. The winner would eventually run in the general election against Democratic State Senator [Leticia Van de Putte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leticia_Van_de_Putte "Leticia Van de Putte") of [San Antonio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Antonio,_Texas "San Antonio, Texas"), who was the Democratic nominee for the lieutenant governorship. During the runoff, Dewhurst released a disco-themed advertisement [Lt. Gov. You've Gotta Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lt._Gov._You've_Gotta_Love "Lt. Gov. You've Gotta Love") and [a parody](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frozen_(advertisement) "Frozen (advertisement)") of [Let It Go](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Let_It_Go_(Disney_song) "Let It Go (Disney song)") from the [Disney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Walt_Disney_Company "The Walt Disney Company") film _[Frozen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frozen\_(2013\_film) "Frozen (2013 film)")_. On May 27, 2014, Patrick easily defeated Dewhurst in a landslide: 65% to 35%.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Dewhurst#cite_note-28)

Patrick said after state Senator [Wendy Davis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wendy_Davis_(politician) "Wendy Davis (politician)") of [Fort Worth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Worth "Fort Worth") (who was the Democratic nominee for governor) [filibustered](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filibuster "Filibuster") the bill to ban late-term abortions in Texas that Dewhurst has "lost his grip on the reins of the Senate". Patrick called for new leadership in the chamber.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Dewhurst#cite_note-davisfilibuster-29)

Polling by the [University of Texas at Austin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Texas_at_Austin "University of Texas at Austin") and _[The Texas Tribune](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Texas\_Tribune "The Texas Tribune")_ showed Dewhurst leading his opponents in the primary with 26 percent of the vote, to Patrick's 13 percent, Patterson's 10 percent and Staples' 5 percent. At the time, 46 percent of voters were reported as undecided.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Dewhurst#cite_note-30)

### Legislation

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=David_Dewhurst&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Legislation")]

#### Childhood legislation

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=David_Dewhurst&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Childhood legislation")]

He is known by his "Texas Children First" initiative[_[clarification needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Please\_clarify "Wikipedia:Please clarify")_] with more severe consequences for child sexual predators in Texas and throughout the [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States "United States").[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Dewhurst#cite_note-31) The initiative includes extending [statute of limitations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statute_of_limitations "Statute of limitations") on child sex crimes and leading the passage of [Jessica's Law](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jessica's_Law "Jessica's Law"). The bill was signed into law by Texas Governor [Rick Perry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Perry "Rick Perry") but the death penalty for second-time child rapists was struck down by the [U.S. Supreme Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Supreme_Court "U.S. Supreme Court").[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Dewhurst#cite_note-32)

#### TSA inspection bill

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=David_Dewhurst&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: TSA inspection bill")]

Dewhurst was accused by state senator Dan Patrick of helping to stop a bill, the passage of which would have been an attempt to make the pat downs of airplane passengers by personnel of the U.S. Transportation Security Agency (TSA) a felony in Texas.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Dewhurst#cite_note-33)

### Controversies

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=David_Dewhurst&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Controversies")]

#### Condemnation of school stage play

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=David_Dewhurst&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Condemnation of school stage play")]

In March 2010, a student performance of the play _[Corpus Christi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corpus\_Christi\_(play) "Corpus Christi (play)")_ by [Terrence McNally](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terrence_McNally "Terrence McNally"), in which Jesus and the disciples are portrayed as being gay, was canceled at [Tarleton State University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tarleton_State_University "Tarleton State University") in [Stephenville, Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephenville,_Texas "Stephenville, Texas") following a condemnatory statement by Dewhurst. The university had received many complaints about the play's scheduled performance as a class project for a directing class, but in a letter posted on the university's website on March 11, President F. Dominic Dottavio, citing freedom of speech, declared that the play would be performed.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Dewhurst#cite_note-34) The day before the performance, Dewhurst issued his statement saying, "No one should have the right to use government funds or institutions to portray acts that are morally reprehensible to the vast majority of Americans," and the performance was cancelled by the professor, who cited safety concerns. A subsequent statement by Dewhurst praised the university for canceling the performance, whereas the professor claimed to have acted on his own. Dewhurst's statement also claimed that whereas he is "a strong defender of free speech, we must also protect the rights and reasonable expectations of Texas taxpayers and how their money is used. A play that is completely contrary to the standards of decency and moral beliefs of the vast majority of Texans should not be performed using any state resources, especially by an institution of higher learning."[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Dewhurst#cite_note-35)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Dewhurst#cite_note-36)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Dewhurst#cite_note-37)

#### Calling Allen, Texas police regarding jailed relative

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=David_Dewhurst&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Calling Allen, Texas police regarding jailed relative")]

In an August 3, 2013, recording, originally released by police to the Dallas-Fort Worth NBC affiliate, NBC-DFW, Dewhurst identifies himself as the lieutenant governor and asks to speak to the police station's "most senior police officer you have where you are right now". He tells a police sergeant that Ellen Bevers, his stepsister's daughter-in-law, is a schoolteacher and "the sweetest woman in the world", and says he's sure she has been incarcerated on a "mistaken charge".[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Dewhurst#cite_note-38)[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Dewhurst#cite_note-39)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Dewhurst#cite_note-40)

## 2012 United States Senate race

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=David_Dewhurst&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: 2012 United States Senate race")]

See also: [United States Senate election in Texas, 2012](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Senate_election_in_Texas,_2012 "United States Senate election in Texas, 2012")

On July 18, 2011, Dewhurst addressed his supporters in an online video on his campaign website, announcing his candidacy for the vacant U.S. Senate seat for the Republican nomination. His rivals included former [Mayor of Dallas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mayor_of_Dallas "Mayor of Dallas")[Tom Leppert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Leppert "Tom Leppert"), [ESPN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ESPN "ESPN") college football analyst [Craig James](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Craig_James_(running_back) "Craig James (running back)") and former state Solicitor General [Ted Cruz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_Cruz "Ted Cruz"), the eventual nominee.

After a year-long campaign for the Republican nomination, Dewhurst lost to Cruz in a run-off on July 31, 2012. Cruz then won the seat in the general election against Democrat [Paul Sadler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Sadler "Paul Sadler") of [Henderson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henderson,_Texas "Henderson, Texas").

**Flavio Delbono** (born 17 September 1959) is an Italian politician and [economist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economist "Economist"). He served as the [mayor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mayor "Mayor") of [Bologna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bologna "Bologna") from 25 June 2009 until 28 January 2010, when he was forced to resign as he was being investigated for crimes such as [embezzlement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Embezzlement "Embezzlement"), [fraud](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fraud "Fraud") and aggravated abuse of office following allegations made by his former lover.

## Biography

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Flavio_Delbono&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Biography")]

Delbono was born in [Sabbioneta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sabbioneta "Sabbioneta"), a small town in the [Province of Mantua](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Province_of_Mantua "Province of Mantua") in [Lombardy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lombardy "Lombardy").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flavio_Delbono#cite_note-ComuneBologna-1) His father was a [municipal policeman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Municipal_police_(Italy) "Municipal police (Italy)") and his mother was a [seamstress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seamstress "Seamstress").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flavio_Delbono#cite_note-ComuneBologna-1) After graduating from the [Liceo scientifico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liceo_scientifico "Liceo scientifico"), Delbono studied economics at the [University of Parma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Parma "University of Parma"), graduating in 1982.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flavio_Delbono#cite_note-ComuneBologna-1) He received a [dottorato di ricerca](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dottorato_di_ricerca "Dottorato di ricerca") in economics from the [University of Siena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Siena "University of Siena") in 1986,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flavio_Delbono#cite_note-LinkedIn-2) and a [D.Phil.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D.Phil. "D.Phil.") from [Linacre College, Oxford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linacre_College,_Oxford "Linacre College, Oxford") in 1988.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flavio_Delbono#cite_note-LinkedIn-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flavio_Delbono#cite_note-Econometrica-3) While at Oxford, Delbono studied under the future [Nobel laureate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Memorial_Prize_in_Economic_Sciences "Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences")[Amartya Sen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amartya_Sen "Amartya Sen").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flavio_Delbono#cite_note-Tiscali-4)

Delbono joined the faculty of the [Johns Hopkins University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johns_Hopkins_University "Johns Hopkins University")[SAIS Bologna Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SAIS_Bologna_Center "SAIS Bologna Center") as an [adjunct professor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adjunct_professor "Adjunct professor") of international economics in 1987.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flavio_Delbono#cite_note-ComuneBologna-1) In 1992, at the age of 33, Delbono was appointed as professor of Political Economy at the [University of Bologna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Bologna "University of Bologna").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flavio_Delbono#cite_note-LinkedIn-2) His predecessors in this position include [Romano Prodi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romano_Prodi "Romano Prodi") and [Stefano Zamagni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stefano_Zamagni "Stefano Zamagni").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flavio_Delbono#cite_note-ComuneBologna-1)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flavio_Delbono#cite_note-JHUGazette-5)

## Political and administrative career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Flavio_Delbono&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Political and administrative career")]

From 1995 to 1999, Delbono served as an [assessor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assessor_(Italy) "Assessor (Italy)") for the city of [Bologna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bologna "Bologna") with specific responsibility for the budget.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flavio_Delbono#cite_note-LinkedIn-2) In 2000, the newly elected President of the [Emilia-Romagna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emilia-Romagna "Emilia-Romagna") region, [Vasco Errani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vasco_Errani "Vasco Errani"), named Delbono as the regional assessor for finance and organisation.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flavio_Delbono#cite_note-ComuneBologna-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flavio_Delbono#cite_note-LinkedIn-2) In 2003 he was also named as vice-president of Emilia-Romagna.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flavio_Delbono#cite_note-ComuneBologna-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flavio_Delbono#cite_note-LinkedIn-2) Following Errani's re-election in May 2005, Delbono was reconfirmed as vice-president and given additional responsibility for the region's relationship with Europe.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flavio_Delbono#cite_note-ComuneBologna-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flavio_Delbono#cite_note-LinkedIn-2)

On 19 June 2008, Delbono was unanimously elected in [Brussels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels "Brussels") as the President of the Lisbon Regions Network—a 15-member pan-European group concerned with implementing the [Lisbon Strategy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lisbon_Strategy "Lisbon Strategy").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flavio_Delbono#cite_note-LisbonRegionsNetwork-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flavio_Delbono#cite_note-Diario-7)

## Primary campaign

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Flavio_Delbono&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Primary campaign")]

On 13 October 2008, Delbono announced his intention to stand in the Democratic Party [primary election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Partisan_primary "Partisan primary") for mayor of Bologna.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flavio_Delbono#cite_note-ETV-8) Delbono's candidacy was backed by several prominent figures in Bolognese politics, including: [Sergio Cofferati](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Cofferati "Sergio Cofferati"),[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flavio_Delbono#cite_note-ETV-8) Romano Prodi,[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flavio_Delbono#cite_note-Prodi-9)[Pier Luigi Bersani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pier_Luigi_Bersani "Pier Luigi Bersani"),[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flavio_Delbono#cite_note-emiliolonardo-10)[Renato Zangheri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renato_Zangheri "Renato Zangheri")[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flavio_Delbono#cite_note-emiliolonardo-10) and [Salvatore Caronna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salvatore_Caronna "Salvatore Caronna").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flavio_Delbono#cite_note-11)

The primary elections took place on 13 and 14 December 2008.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flavio_Delbono#cite_note-primarydate-12) Delbono received 49.73% of the 24,920 votes cast in the primary; Maurizio Cevenini received 23.29%, Virginio Merola received 21.44% and Andrea Forlani received 5.1%.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flavio_Delbono#cite_note-unita-13)

## Campaign for mayor of Bologna

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Flavio_Delbono&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Campaign for mayor of Bologna")]

On 9 January 2009, Delbono announced that he would be resigning as vice-president of Emilia-Romagna and regional assessor in order to focus on his election campaign.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flavio_Delbono#cite_note-wordpress-14) Maria Giuseppina Muzzarelli was announced as his successor as vice-president on 3 February.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flavio_Delbono#cite_note-Errani-15) The mayoral election was held on 21 and 22 June; Delbono's opponents included [Alfredo Cazzola](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfredo_Cazzola?action=edit&redlink=1 "Alfredo Cazzola (page does not exist)"), the candidate of [The People of Freedom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_People_of_Freedom "The People of Freedom") and [Lega Nord](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lega_Nord "Lega Nord"), and the [UDC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Union_of_the_Centre_(2008) "Union of the Centre (2008)")'s [Giorgio Guazzaloca](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giorgio_Guazzaloca "Giorgio Guazzaloca"), a former mayor of Bologna.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flavio_Delbono#cite_note-election-16) Delbono received 49.4% of the vote in the first round, forcing a [second round](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Two-round_system "Two-round system") against Cazzola, who had received 29.1%.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flavio_Delbono#cite_note-election-16) Delbono received 60.67% of the votes in the second round.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flavio_Delbono#cite_note-election-16) Delbono was officially proclaimed as mayor of the city of Bologna on 25 June 2009.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flavio_Delbono#cite_note-17)

## Scandal and resignation

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Flavio_Delbono&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Scandal and resignation")]

Delbono was forced to announce his resignation as mayor on 25 January 2010 following the revelation that he was being investigated for crimes such as [embezzlement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Embezzlement "Embezzlement"), [fraud](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fraud "Fraud") and aggravated abuse of office.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flavio_Delbono#cite_note-Economist-18) The investigation followed Delbono's former assistant's claim that he had spent public money on her— the pair had been having an affair.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flavio_Delbono#cite_note-Economist-18) Investigators subsequently questioned Delbono about the purchase of a property near [St. Julian's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Julian's "St. Julian's"), [Malta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malta "Malta").[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flavio_Delbono#cite_note-Malta-19) Delbono denied all the allegations made against him and said that resigning as mayor was the right thing to do.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flavio_Delbono#cite_note-Economist-18)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flavio_Delbono#cite_note-Malta-19) He has announced that he will return to lecturing and is working to clear his name.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flavio_Delbono#cite_note-Malta-19) His resignation was confirmed on 28 January following the approval of an emergency budget, the election to appoint Delbono's successor must take place by 28 March 2010.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flavio_Delbono#cite_note-resignation-20)

However, [Bologna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bologna "Bologna") did not receive a mayor until 2011, and was ruled by a commissioner, [Anna Maria Cancellieri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anna_Maria_Cancellieri "Anna Maria Cancellieri").
